claim: Huguet et al. 2025 report a single-site UWB indoor-positioning study of consenting ED staff at Le Corbusier Hospital, Firminy, France, from 7 March to 21 April 2022. The article's Methods defines an hourly walking-distance measure by calculating planar Euclidean (as-the-crow-flies) distance between locations from the same tag and aggregating the resulting distances per hour, in metres. This is a location-derived displacement measure; the article does not define a traversable operational route graph, graph revision, edge or access classes, route/movement-mode restrictions, reachable origin/destination set, obstacle-constrained path, or route-choice policy. Its location and distance results are specific to one ED and are not a generic route policy. R5 describes the distance as successive same-tag coordinate displacements, but the located primary-source paragraph says only points of the same tag; this record does not attribute the word 'successive' to the article. Consequently, hourly Euclidean displacement must not be treated as route connectivity, route length, walking speed, or a default route rule. Graph topology, access constraints, movement-mode reachability, and route choice remain unknown. No route coefficient, distribution, universal heuristic, empirical default, or model calibration target is established by this record.

primary_source.population: Consenting healthcare professionals wearing anonymized UWB tags at Le Corbusier Hospital emergency department, Firminy, France. The article reports 27 tags associated with eight staff-type labels; no patients are tracked in this movement measure.
primary_source.units: Hourly aggregated same-tag planar Euclidean displacement in metres. It is not a reported route length, origin-destination trip distance, or walking-speed distribution.
